from fractions import Fraction as F

# Model: wearing less raises arthritis risk (Zhang's causal claim holds),
# yet people who wear more also get arthritis (age etc. are other causes).
# If this model makes option D true, D does not refute the causal claim.

# Population: age group (young/old) x clothing (less/more); risk values
risk = {
    ("young", "less"): F(3, 10),
    ("young", "more"): F(1, 10),
    ("old", "less"): F(7, 10),
    ("old", "more"): F(5, 10),
}
# Wearing less raises risk within every age group -> causal claim true in model
causal_holds = all(risk[(a, "less")] > risk[(a, "more")] for a in ("young", "old"))

# Option D: many who wear more get arthritis, mostly middle-aged/elderly
pop_more = {"young": 1000, "old": 1000}
cases_more = {a: pop_more[a] * risk[(a, "more")] for a in pop_more}
total_cases_more = sum(cases_more.values())
D_true_in_model = total_cases_more > 0 and cases_more["old"] > cases_more["young"]

print("causal claim holds in model:", causal_holds)
print("cases among those wearing more:", cases_more, "total", total_cases_more)
print("option D true in the same model:", D_true_in_model)

if causal_holds and D_true_in_model:
    print("D is fully consistent with Zhang's causal claim, so it does not undermine it.")
    print("Option C (same city, same habit, same exposure, no arthritis) is the stronger challenge.")
    print("CHECK FAIL")
else:
    print("CHECK PASS")
